{{Short description|Italian physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}
'''Ignazio Ciufolini''' (born 1951) is an Italian physicist active in the field of [[gravitational physics]] and [[general relativity]].

==Biography==
Ignazio Ciufolini graduated magna cum laude in 1980 at Sapienza University of Rome, and received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics in 1984 at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] under the supervision of [[Richard Matzner]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Clippard|first=Lee|title=UT Researchers Send Experimental Satellite into Space|url=http://alcalde.texasexes.org/2012/02/ut-researchers-send-experimental-satellite-into-space/|work=[[The Alcalde]]|date=20 February 2012|accessdate=9 January 2014}}</ref><!-- 404 ERROR <ref>{{cite web|title=Ignazio Ciufolini, PhD Thesis Title with Signatures|url=http://www.lares-mission.com/downloadable/Ciufolini_PhDcommittee.png|accessdate=9 January 2014}}</ref>-->

From 1982 to 1988, he worked at University of Texas at Austin as a teaching assistant, lecturer and research associate. As of 2014, he is an associate professor of general physics at [[University of Salento]] (Italy),<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignazio Ciufolini personal card|url=https://www.ingegneria.unisalento.it/scheda_personale/-/people/ignazio.ciufolini|accessdate=9 January 2014|language=it|archive-date=9 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109171424/https://www.ingegneria.unisalento.it/scheda_personale/-/people/ignazio.ciufolini|url-status=dead}}</ref> tenured since 1999, and a member of Centro Fermi, Rome.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignazio Ciufolini personal page on Centro Studi e Ricerche Enrico Fermi web site|url=http://www.centrofermi.it/index.php/component/content/article/22-english/152-ciufolinis|accessdate=9 January 2014|archive-date=9 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109174450/http://www.centrofermi.it/index.php/component/content/article/22-english/152-ciufolinis|url-status=dead}}</ref> He collaborated with John Archibald Wheeler in 1995 to write ''Gravitation and Inertia'',<ref>Ignazio Ciufolini and John Archibald Wheeler. ''Gravitation and Inertia''. Princeton University Press. Princeton, New Jersey (1995). {{ISBN|0-691-03323-4}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Schucking, Engelbert Levin|author-link=Engelbert Schücking|title=Review of ''Gravitation and Inertia'' by Ignazio Ciufolini and John A. Wheeler|journal=Physics Today|volume=49|issue=6|year=1996|page=58|bibcode=1996PhT....49f..58C|doi=10.1063/1.2807658|s2cid=120135060 }}</ref> for which they won the [[PROSE Awards|PROSE Award]] for the best professional and scholar book in physics and astronomy.<ref>{{cite web|title=AAP PROSE Awards 1995 Winners.  |url=http://pspcentral.org/rtAwards/attachArchive/winners_95.rtf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110825065056/http://pspcentral.org/rtAwards/attachArchive/winners_95.rtf|url-status=usurped|archive-date=25 August 2011}}</ref> He works mainly in the field of General Relativity and Gravitational Physics, proposing a method to measure the effects of [[Gravitoelectromagnetism|gravitomagnetism]] using the data from the [[laser ranging|laser ranged]] satellites [[LAGEOS]] and LAGEOS-2.<ref name=Nature>

In 2010, he won the [[Giuseppe Occhialini Medal and Prize]], jointly awarded by the [[Italian Physical Society]] and the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/occhialini/medallists/page_38497.html#gref |title=Occhialini medal recipients |website=iop.org |publisher=Institute of Physics |accessdate=13 February 2020}}</ref>

In 2014, Ciufolini was accused<ref>{{cite journal |arxiv=1407.2137|last1=Iorio|first1=L.|journal=Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology |volume=65 |issue=11 |page=2375 |doi=10.1002/asi.23238 |title=''Withdrawal:'' 'A new type of misconduct in the field of the physical sciences: The case of the pseudonyms used by I. Ciufolini to anonymously criticize other people's works on arXiv' by L. Iorio|year=2014}}{{Retracted|doi=10.1002/asi.23238|intentional=yes}}</ref> of publishing papers on the scientific pre-print archive [[arXiv]] under pseudonyms, such as G. Felici<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=gr-qc/0703020|last1=Felici|first1=G.|title=The meaning of systematic errors, a comment to "Reply to on the Systematic Errors in the Detection of the Lense-Thirring Effect with a Mars Orbiter", by Lorenzo Iorio|year=2007 }}</ref> and G. Forst,<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=0712.3934|last1=Forst|first1=G.|title=A critical analysis of the GP-B mission. I: On the impossibility of a reliable measurement of the gravitomagnetic precession of the GP-B gyroscopes|year=2007|class=gr-qc}}</ref> which is a violation of the [[arXiv]] terms.<ref name="RW1">{{cite news|title=Journal retracts letter accusing physicist of using fake names to criticize papers|author=Retraction Watch|date=3 June 2014|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2014/06/03/journal-retracts-letter-accusing-physicist-of-using-fake-names-to-criticize-papers-on-arxiv/|accessdate=24 May 2019|author-link=Retraction Watch}}</ref><ref name="RW2">{{cite news|title=Retraction of letter alleging sock puppetry now cites "legal reasons"|author=Retraction Watch|date=16 June 2014|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2014/06/16/retraction-of-letter-alleging-sock-puppetry-now-cites-legal-reasons/|accessdate=24 May 2019|author-link=Retraction Watch}}</ref><ref name="one">{{cite news|title=Science Pseudonyms vs Science Sockpuppets|author=Neuroskeptic|date=10 May 2014|url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/mind/science-pseudonyms-vs-science-sockpuppets|accessdate=25 October 2023|author-link=Neuroskeptic}}</ref><ref name="two">{{cite news|title=Ignazio Ciufolini detto G. Forst detto G. Felici|author=Sylvie Coyaud|date=10 May 2014|language=it|url=https://archivio.ocasapiens.org/index.php/2014/05/10/ignazio-ciufolini-detto-g-forst-detto-g-felici/|accessdate=27 May 2026}}</ref> For this and other reasons, Ciufolini twice sued physicist Lorenzo Iorio for defamation, but he was acquitted in both cases.<ref name="RW3">{{cite news|title=Spat between physicists hits Italian courts for the second time|date=13 January 2015|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2015/01/13/spat-physicists-hits-italian-courts-second-time/|accessdate=24 May 2026|author-link=Retraction Watch}}</ref> Not satisfied, Ciufolini sued Iorio for damages in civil court, winning the case this time.<ref name="RW4">{{cite news|title=Feud between physicists ends in defamation verdict|date=19 May 2026|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2026/05/19/feud-between-physicists-ends-in-defamation-verdict/|accessdate=24 May 2026|author-link=Retraction Watch}}</ref>
